name: Top-level ontologies, Part 1: Requirements
uses: What makes an ontology top-level: domain neutral, with the most general categories that domain ontologies specialize. It names the layer Naive's five top categories sit on, and Part 2 is BFO.
note: Not confirmed at its url from this session; the identifier is cited from BFO's documentation, which names ISO/IEC 21838-2 as Part 2 of this series. The ISO text is restricted.
